assessments.support: This dataset consists 1,035 rs-fMRI data with 505 ASD subject, and 530 healthy control subjects that are collected from 17 diﬀerent sites.

We used the preprocessed data using the Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes C-PAC pipeline (Craddock et al., 2013) Craddock 200 (CC200) functional parcellation (Craddock et al., 2012)
ASD/HC labels taken from ABIDE's own site diagnoses; no ADOS/ADI-R criterion or diagnosis-validation procedure described in this paper.

k-fold cross-validation is described only generically ("the dataset is randomly split into k equal sized samples"); it is not explicitly stated whether the sparse-autoencoder/classifier was retrained from scratch within each fold or whether any feature-wise preprocessing was confined to training folds. No site covariate or harmonization is applied in the whole-dataset model; per-site 5-fold CV evaluates generalizability across sites but is not a leave-one-site-out test.

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort and pipeline (C-PAC, CC200, 17 sites) are clearly reported, but cross-validation leakage control is not explicitly described and no site-harmonisation or leave-site-out evaluation is used for the main whole-dataset model.

charting.title: ASD-SAENet: A Sparse Autoencoder, and Deep-Neural Network Model for Detecting Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using fMRI Data
charting.primary_goal: Classify ASD vs healthy control using a sparse-autoencoder deep-neural-network model on ABIDE-I resting-state functional connectivity.
charting.dataset_openly_available: The implemented code is available on GitHub portal of our lab at: https:// github.com/pcdslab/ASD-SAENet.
charting.feature_types: Pairwise functional connectivity (Pearson correlation) between CC200 ROIs
charting.specific_features: Pearson correlation functional connectivity matrix over 200 CC200 regions
charting.specific_algorithms: Sparse autoencoder (feature reduction) jointly trained with a two-hidden-layer softmax DNN classifier (ASD-SAENet)
charting.validation_methodology: 10-fold cross-validation on the whole ABIDE-I dataset; separate 5-fold cross-validation per site
charting.key_performance_results: ASD-SAENet exhibits comparable accuracy (70.8%), and superior speciﬁcity (79.1%) for the whole dataset as compared to other methods. exhibits better accuracy for 12 out of the 17 sites. The average accuracy achieved by ASD-SAENet model was 64.42%
charting.summary_key_findings: ASD-SAENet achieved 70.8% accuracy and 79.1% specificity on the whole ABIDE-I dataset (10-fold CV), comparable to prior state-of-the-art methods but with substantially shorter training time, and outperformed comparators on 12 of 17 individual sites (average per-site accuracy 64.42%, 5-fold CV).

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE-I, 17 sites, 1035 subjects (505 ASD/530 HC)
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed CC200 functional connectivity, sparse autoencoder jointly trained with a two-layer softmax DNN classifier (ASD-SAENet); 10-fold CV on whole dataset and separate per-site 5-fold CV.
narrative_row.outcomes: 70.8% accuracy and 79.1% specificity on the whole dataset (comparable to prior state-of-the-art but faster to train); outperformed comparators on 12/17 sites with 64.42% average per-site accuracy.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Cross-validation leakage control not explicitly described; no site harmonisation or leave-one-site-out test for the pooled model; per-site models limited by small site-level sample sizes.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Benchmarks a lightweight sparse-autoencoder classifier against prior ABIDE-I deep-learning baselines (ASD-DiagNet, Heinsfeld et al.) using the same C-PAC/CC200 preprocessing, with code released on GitHub.
